introduction: Tailored for UGC NET and advanced educational leadership exams, this level dissects the newest bodies created by NEP 2020 (like PARAKH), the advanced frameworks for teacher education (NCF-TE), and the nuances of institutional accreditation.

core_concepts.title: PARAKH (National Assessment Centre)
core_concepts.description:
Performance Assessment, Review, and Analysis of Knowledge for Holistic Development.
- Setup: A newly established standard-setting body under **NCERT**.
- Mandate: To guide all recognized school boards in India (CBSE, ICSE, State Boards). Its goal is to end the disparity between different boards by establishing uniform norms, standards, and guidelines for student assessment, specifically shifting assessments toward 21st-century competencies.

core_concepts.title: NCF-TE (National Curriculum Framework for Teacher Education)
core_concepts.description:
While NCERT creates the curriculum for children, NCTE creates the curriculum for teachers.
- NEP 2020 mandate: NCTE must formulate a new NCF-TE (2021) in consultation with NCERT.
- The 4-Year ITEP: NCF-TE officially transitions teacher education away from standalone 2-year B.Ed. degrees to the 4-year Integrated Teacher Education Programme (ITEP) (e.g., B.A.B.Ed., B.Sc.B.Ed.) offered exclusively in multidisciplinary universities by 2030, shutting down isolated 'sub-standard' teacher training colleges.

core_concepts.title: Institutional Accreditation: SQAAF
core_concepts.description:
School Quality Assessment and Assurance Framework (SQAAF).
- NEP 2020 mandates that all schools (public and private) must be periodically assessed and accredited.
- The State School Standards Authority (SSSA) will use the SQAAF framework to assess schools on parameters like curriculum, infrastructure, safety, and inclusive practices, ensuring public transparency regarding school quality.

core_concepts.title: NIEPA's Advanced Leadership Programs
core_concepts.description: At the highest level of systemic reform, NIEPA conducts the **NCSL (National Centre for School Leadership)** program. Recognizing that a school is only as good as its principal, NCSL provides intensive leadership training to Head Teachers, shifting their role from mere 'administrators' to 'pedagogical leaders' capable of driving change and implementing CBE.

important_entities.name: State Quality Assessment and Accreditation (SQAA)
important_entities.significance: Historically, Indian schools faced corrupt 'inspectors'. NEP 2020 replaces this with SQAA—a system of public self-disclosure where schools upload their own data on infrastructure and outcomes, followed by randomized external audits, ensuring accountability through public transparency.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners will claim: 'PARAKH is an independent constitutional body.' This is **FALSE**. PARAKH is a constituent unit operating *under* NCERT. It is powerful, but it is not a standalone ministry or constitutional body.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: NCF-SE by NCERT; NCF-TE by NCTE
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: SE = School Education (done by NCERT). TE = Teacher Education (done by NCTE in consultation with NCERT).

exam_strategy_tips: If an advanced DSSSB question asks 'By 2030, which degree will be the minimum qualification for school teachers according to NCTE?', select the **4-year Integrated Teacher Education Programme (ITEP)**.
